descriptionChirho: The indeclinable proper noun Ἰωσήφ (Iōsēph) referring to various biblical figures named Joseph — including the OT patriarch, Jesus' earthly father, Joseph of Arimathea, and Joseph Barnabas. Appears across all case functions (35x) with consistent multilingual rendering: Spanish 'Iōsḗph,' Hindi 'यूसुफ,' Arabic 'يوسف,' Korean '요셉,' Swahili 'Iōsḗph.' This is the standard form used throughout the NT for this well-known Semitic name.

A variant proper noun form Ἰωσήχ (Iōsēch), appearing once in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3:26), referring to an otherwise unknown ancestor. Distinguished from the common 'Iōsēph' by its final consonant (-ch vs -ph), reflected in multilingual transliterations: Spanish 'Iōsēch,' Hindi 'योसेख,' Arabic 'يوسيخ,' Korean '요섹,' Swahili 'Iōsēch.' This is a distinct onomastic entry, not merely a case variant of the common Joseph.
